clause.text:
1. Business Cooperation

Party A and Party B unanimously agree that the proposed cooperation shall be the internet-based sale and promotion of tour products conducted by Party A and its subsidiaries or other value-added business carried out by Party A. Party B shall provide the business consultancy and technical services as well as the technical consultancy as set forth in Article 3 hereinafter to Party A and its subsidiaries to facilitate them to conduct the aforementioned business and supply relevant products and services.
clause.heading: 1. Business Cooperation

reviews.rationale: The clause merely outlines cooperation for internet-based sale and promotion of tour products and the provision of consultancy and technical services. It does not impose any non‑compete restrictions, which aligns with the playbook position that parties are not restricted from competing. Hence the clause is consistent with the preferred non‑compete language and does not raise additional risk.

citations.excerpt: Neither party is restricted from competing with the other or from operating in any geography, business or technology sector during or after the Term.

clause.text: 2. Exclusive Cooperation
clause.heading: 2. Exclusive Cooperation

reviews.rationale: The clause title "Exclusive Cooperation" implies an exclusivity commitment, which directly conflicts with the company's playbook position that mandates non‑exclusive dealing. The playbook explicitly states the agreement must be non‑exclusive, allowing each party to engage with third parties freely. This mismatch creates a high risk that the clause would impose unwelcome exclusivity obligations.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is non-exclusive. Each party remains free to provide to, procure from, or contract with any third party for services of the same or a similar kind, without restriction and without any obligation to the other party.

Party A shall not establish any same or similar cooperative relationship with any third party in respect of such businesses nor shall it make any same or similar arrangement, unless with the prior written consent of Party B.

The playbook explicitly states that the agreement must be non‑exclusive, allowing each party to freely contract with third parties for similar services. This contradiction creates significant contractual risk, as it may expose the company to breach claims and limit flexibility. The appropriate fallback language is the playbook's preferred non‑exclusive wording.

clause.text: 4. Cooperation Remuneration
clause.heading: 4. Cooperation Remuneration

reviews.rationale: The clause provides no definition, calculation method, timing, or reporting requirements for the cooperation remuneration. According to the playbook, a proper payment‑terms clause must define the revenue share on net revenue, state the percentage, and require payment within 30 days of each calendar quarter with a calculation statement (revenue-share-defined). The absence of these elements represents a deviation from the preferred position and therefore carries the medium risk indicated by the playbook.

citations.excerpt: Any revenue or profit share payable under this Agreement shall be calculated on net revenue actually received, at the percentage stated in the Order Form, and shall be payable within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter together with a statement showing the calculation.

clause.text:
4.1 Party A and Party B unanimously agree that they will allocate the proceeds generated from cooperation in accordance with thefollowing provisions:

Party B shall have the right to charge, on a quarterly basis, the service fee ("Service Fee") from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services, or designate another person to charge Service Fee from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. The total sum of Service Fee shall be equal to the amount of profits gained by Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. Party B shall have the right to adjust the amount of Service Fee at its own discretion, without the prior consent of Party A or its subsidiaries.

Party A shall cause its subsidiaries to pay the Service Fee in respect of Party B's Services provided to such subsidiaries.
clause.heading: 4.1 Party A and Party B unanimously agree that they will allocate the proceeds generated from cooperation in accordance with thefollowing provisions:

reviews.rationale: The clause grants Party B unilateral discretion to adjust the Service Fee without Party A's prior consent, which creates an imbalance and exposes Party A to unpredictable costs. The playbook’s assignment position requires prior written consent for changes, indicating that such unilateral financial adjustments are contrary to the company's standard of mutual consent for material modifications.

citations.excerpt: Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except that either party may assign it in its entirety, on notice and without consent, to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.

clause.text: 4.2 The Service Fee of the last quarter shall be paid prior to the seventh business day following the commencement of the next quarter. Such Service Fee shall be paid to the bank account designated by Party B in writing. If Party B intends to change its bank account, it shall send a written notice to Party A seven business days in advance.
clause.heading: 4.2 The Service Fee of the last quarter shall be paid prior to the seventh business day following the commencement of the next quarter. Such Service Fee shall be paid to the bank account designated by Party B in writing. If Party B intends to change its bank account, it shall send a written notice to Party A seven business days in advance.

reviews.rationale: The clause sets a payment deadline of the seventh business day after the start of the next quarter and requires a seven‑business‑day notice for bank‑account changes. The playbook’s payment‑terms position (revenue-share-defined) specifies that payments should be made within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter. The clause’s timing is stricter (earlier) than the playbook’s preferred schedule, which does not create a conflict and actually benefits the payee by ensuring prompt payment. The notice requirement for bank‑account changes is reasonable and not addressed in the playbook, so it does not introduce additional risk. Consequently, the clause aligns with the company’s expectations and poses low risk.

clause.heading: 4.3 Except as otherwise agreed hereunder, if Party A or its subsidiaries fail to pay the Service Fee in full on schedule according to provisions of Article 4.1 and Article 4.2, then Party A or its subsidiaries shall, in addition to the continuance of the payment of Service Fee in full, it shall pay Party B the liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.03% in respect of the outstanding Service Fee.

clause.text:
5. Term of Cooperation

Party A and Party B agree and confirm that the term of cooperation under this Agreement shall commence from the execution date hereof and end on the expiration date of the operation term of Party B ("Term of Cooperation").
clause.heading: 5. Term of Cooperation

reviews.rationale: The clause only defines the initial term of cooperation and does not address renewal or termination for convenience. The company's playbook requires an opt‑in renewal provision (renewal‑opt‑in) and a termination‑for‑convenience clause. The absence of these mechanisms increases contractual risk because the agreement would automatically continue without mutual consent and lacks a clear exit right.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term and shall renew only if both parties agree in writing to renew it. Any renewal term shall not exceed twelve (12) months.

Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party, without penalty or further liability other than for amounts accrued prior to the effective date of termination.

clause.heading: 6. Termination

The playbook position [post-termination-wind-down] states that on termination each party's obligations cease except for those that expressly survive and provides a bounded transition assistance period, indicating that without such language the risk is not low.
